we have developed the most effective method for the enantioselective total synthesis of EGCG, the active polyphenolic component from green tea.

the synthesis of EGCG was achieved by the following three steps: (1) the synthesis of the key intermediate (7c), (2) the stereospecific cyclisation of 7c to 9c, and (3) the deprotection of the cyclized product 9c to EGCG.

the synthesis of 3b can be accomplished in only 5 steps and 15% overall yield.
it is possible to synthesize the natural enantiomers of the green tea polyphenol epigallocatechin gallate (EGCG) and the synthetic EGCG enantiomers are not toxic.
the enantioselectivity of the cyclization reaction is controlled by the stereochemistry of the diol functionality, and that the cyclization proceeds with high stereospecificity and stereoselectivity.
